q: What is the key difference between the reaction centre and the other pigment molecules in a photosystem?
options: Only the reaction centre absorbs light; the antenna pigments are colourless proteins that hold it in place
Only the reaction centre emits excited electrons to an acceptor; antenna pigments just pass energy on
The reaction centre contains only carotenoids, whereas antenna pigments are all chlorophyll a
The reaction centre makes ATP directly when excited, whereas the antenna makes NADPH
explanation: Antenna (light-harvesting) complexes contain hundreds of pigment molecules – chlorophyll a and b and carotenoids – that funnel energy inwards. The reaction centre is a special pair of chlorophyll a molecules (P680 in PSII, P700 in PSI) held by proteins next to a primary electron acceptor, so it can donate an excited electron. It is then left oxidised (P680+ or P700+) and must be refilled.
